decisions.statement: serverless workloads scale to zero when idle
every pull request names what it deletes
every GitHub artifact, code comment and document is written in English, the default locale of every site; only a translation catalog of another locale holds that locale's text
before 1.0, a feature that breaks nothing ships in a patch, and only a breaking change makes a minor
with a support catalog, only a commit that touches a project the catalog lists as stable, or an unlisted project a stable one depends on, advances its version line past a patch
the core CLI declares no development verb: build, test, lint, serve, run, format, package, publish, deploy, generate and validate come from @putnami/dev, which the language extensions depend on
there is no kit or profile concept: installing an extension installs its extensionDependencies, and that graph decides what a workspace gets
putnami init --extension <language> installs that language extension, and its dependencies bring the rest
anonymous usage telemetry stays in the core CLI
the core CLI computes a tree's version before any cache key; the version get|tag and changelog commands belong to @putnami/dev
@putnami/contributor ships a compiled executable and owns change verify|finalize|language
@putnami/dev does not depend on @putnami/contributor, which installs only on explicit request: a workspace receives the contributor skills and agents only when someone asks for @putnami/contributor
putnami migrate agent-content is deleted in the next minor release, with no transition window
an extension command calls the collaboration providers through an RPC call to the core, made with an SDK client
the planner and the scheduler are packages, and import paths set the engine boundary: only internal/engine names planner.Plan and scheduler.RunPlan
the change noun carries the change workflow: change verify, change finalize and change language replace tree verify, proposals finalize and contributor language
sessions export and sessions summary stay in the core, because they read the host's session store
@putnami/dev owns the version noun; version list|use, which list and switch the installed CLI binaries, become cli list|use
contributor machine-load becomes doctor --machine, in the core
the core's dev noun is deleted: dev extension validate becomes extensions validate <path>, and dev template <action> becomes templates validate|test|package <path>
an extension manifest declares the kind of each command it adds, in an additive contract rung that ships with the traits that replace verb-name checks
a feature declaration may list the commands that carry the feature

Cloud deletes its nine alias subcommands (tokens, distribution, oci, publish-archives, track, report, validate-config, publish-config, publish-migration) in a dedicated Cloud pull request that ships as a breaking Cloud release

publication uploads to the Putnami registries go through the @putnami/cloud uploader, which can optimize transfer and cost; a publication job uploads to any other registry itself, with its environment's credentials

every workspace project carries a feature of its own, a spec or a reviewed featureAuthority; validate-workspace fails a project that carries none unless the committed debt list names it, and that list only shrinks

a protocol owns the feature of its contract and the contract's functional requirements; each project that implements the protocol depends on it and proves those requirements in its own tests, under a check of its own
a change runs one loop of stages, talk, declare, show, code, check, prove, validate and merge; no other list of stages exists, and deployment after merge is CI/CD, not a stage
an issue is delivered by one pull request with no line or time cap; several pull requests mean several issues, grouped in an epic that orders them
the slices of one issue run in sequence in the main session; parallel work means several issues of an epic, and by default only review runs in a subagent

code starts without the owner's approval unless the plan spans several slices with important design or spec decisions, or touches a sensitive zone; then the owner approves the study and a cost envelope first
a project declares its sensitive zones in SDD; for a project that declares none, data migrations and the public API are its sensitive zones
the issue holds the intent and labels, the mission holds the live state, the pull request description is the archive, and a change's screenshots and reports live under .putnami/, outside Git
an issue carries type/, priority/ (urgent, high, normal, low) and scope/ labels, and workflow/<profile> selects a workflow profile; P1 to P3 name review finding severity only

a workflow profile becomes the default for an issue type only after five paired runs on the same base show a lower total cost, a lower cost in at least four of the five pairs, no more P1 or P2 findings and no more rework

build runs the default workflow profile unless --profile or the issue's workflow label selects another; the default profile runs every loop stage in the main session and only review in a separate agent
an epic session plans issues in dependency order, launches one build session per issue in waves under one epic envelope the owner approves, and never codes
a child issue stacks on at most one unmerged parent whose proposal is ready, and after the parent's squash merge rebases with git rebase --onto <base> <parent's last head>
the 0.4.0 release tags every version line at 0.4.0, each with its explicit tag, whatever version the line computes; D-004 and D-005 keep deciding every later release

an external spec file in a market format (OpenSpec, Spec Kit, Kiro, Gherkin) can be the one home of a feature's outcomes, non-goals and requirement texts; a reader projects it in memory into the native spec, and no command commits that projection as JSON

a feature exists only through its declaration in putnami.features.json or Module.Feature; its putnami.features.json entry names its external spec by format and path, and a spec folder never creates a feature

verification checks, thresholds and windows are authored in putnami.features.json; scenarios in an external spec are compared with the declared checks and a mismatch either way is a warning, never a change to the check set
a requirement ID survives reordering: a name-based ID is accepted after kebab normalization, and a positional ID such as FR-001 or 1.1 needs an explicit anchor before its project can enforce specs

a spec reader ignores an unknown section and warns on a derived-fact section; an external text over the 512-byte bound is still read, with a finding that names a split and blocks only in enforce; a native spec keeps the bound as an error
decisions.settledBy: the epic session, under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-05

decisions.statement: only doc/adr/*.md links are decisions; design.md and plan.md are context, never decision links
native and external specs are discovered together, so one spec per feature covers both and a feature with both fails specs validate

specs init <feature> --from <format>:<path> writes one new native spec with O_EXCL, supports --dry-run, carries only text copied from the source, and has no --all and no --force; there is no specs migrate
a project lists the market spec formats it reads in options.sdd.specFormats, empty by default
a manifest that names a spec format its project did not opt into fails specs validate in every verification mode, and the file is not read
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: options.sdd.specFormats resolves as the project's list, then the workspace's, then empty; a project's list replaces the workspace's
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a spec reader reads only .md and .feature files, and the spec tasks key them through git:**/*.md and git:**/*.feature
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a format whose scenarios belong to the file, not to one requirement, compares them with every check its requirements declare; a mismatch either way stays a warning
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a Kiro acceptance criterion is one native requirement whose ID is its anchor, else <group>-<ordinal>; a group anchor names its criteria but pins none, so each criterion needs its own anchor under enforce
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a Kiro criterion in no EARS form stays in the projection with a warning at its line, and the FOR ALL property counts as a recognized form
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a Kiro Introduction paragraph over the 512-byte bound is cut at sentence ends into several outcomes; a single sentence over the bound stays whole, under D-043
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: the Gherkin reader uses the standard library and the upstream keyword table of cucumber/gherkin committed as data, so protocols/features gains no third-party module; a new upstream language is a data update
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: specs init --from reads only the external spec the feature's manifest entry names, through the discovery the gate uses, and refuses a source whose projection enforce would refuse
decisions.settledBy: a build session, for the owner to review on its proposal

decisions.statement: a requirement name maps to an ID through NFKD less combining marks, then each run of characters other than ASCII letters and digits becomes one hyphen; a name with nothing left or over 128 bytes takes requirement-<ordinal> and is unanchored
decisions.settledBy: the epic session, under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-05

decisions.statement: a workflow unit with no requirement is current, passes every final check without a producer proof and closes its task; it is refused when the change edits a spec or a feature manifest
decisions.settledBy: the epic session, under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-05

decisions.statement: this workspace binds the missions contract to @putnami/intelligence, the only installed provider whose missions.status reads the sessions of every worktree; @putnami/local-collaboration keeps one store per worktree
decisions.settledBy: the epic session, under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-05

decisions.statement: a cloud child of an epic runs build in push-only mode and opens no proposal; the epic session reviews and gates its pushed head in a local worktree, then publishes its proposal, and opens no proposal for a local child
decisions.settledBy: the epic session, under the owner's delegation of 2026-11-05

decisions.statement: architecture import --from structurizr makes each container a domain <system>/<container> and a container-less system a domain <system>; a domain pair with no import gets one reference import of the producer's generated or single reference export
decisions.settledBy: the owner, approving the Structurizr import plan

decisions.statement: architecture import writes only with --apply and then only adds manifests, projects, exports, imports and bindings; it never changes or removes an existing entry, so a hand edit survives a rerun
decisions.settledBy: the owner, approving the Structurizr import plan

decisions.statement: a monorepo tool integration, such as @putnami/bazel or @putnami/pants, lives in monorepo/<tool>, a top-level scope of its own, never under tooling/

putnami init --from <tool> adopts in one of two modes, import or delegate: in a terminal it asks with import preselected, without a terminal it imports unless --mode delegate is given, and --mode import|delegate skips the question

an adoption in import mode lets Putnami install the dependencies: the language extension writes the root manifest of its package manager and installs, and the tool's own lockfile and installer are no longer used

an import adopts Putnami's TypeScript conventions: a project whose main names a build output gains exports ./src/index.ts, and a project without tsconfig.json gets one that extends the root; each rewrite is listed and shown in the rerun diff
